program_name: Master in Accounting and Finance. This is the official English name used on the unibz programme page, on the 2026/27 brochure cover and on the 2026/27 admission-information document. The programme is legally issued in three languages and the other two official names matter because the binding administrative acts (the signed ranking-list decrees) are published ONLY in Italian and German, never in English: Italian 'Laurea magistrale in Accounting e Finanza' and German 'Master in Accounting und Finanzwirtschaft'. Faculty: Faculty of Economics and Management (Fakultaet fuer Wirtschaftswissenschaften / Facolta di Economia). Degree awarded: Laurea Magistrale (second-cycle degree, 120 ECTS, 2 years). Degree Course Director: Prof. Paolo Perego (who also chairs the admission committee and signs the ranking lists as 'Il Presidente / Der Vorsitzender'). Admission committee members named on the 2026/27 decrees: Prof. Nicola Dalla Via and Prof. Massimiliano Bonacchi. Student Representative in the Course Council: Giada Mantovani. Do not confuse this programme with the unibz PhD in Economics and Finance (a separate doctoral programme at the same faculty) or with the Master in Data Analytics for Economics and Management / Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation, which are the English-taught masters of the same faculty.
level: Master (second cycle / laurea magistrale / Masterstudium). 120 ECTS credit points over 2 years (4 semesters). Italian second-cycle degree in class LM-77. Not a single-cycle programme, not a professional/first-level 'Master universitario' (the faculty runs those separately, e.g. the 1st Level Master in Digital and Socially Sustainable Human Resources Management). The programme qualifies for admission to post-graduate training including PhD programmes: 'This study programme also qualifies to gain admission to post-graduate training, such as a PhD programme.' Simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 programmes is allowed under national law, provided the two programmes are not in the same degree class and differ by at least 2/3 of the course contents.
teaching_language: TRILINGUAL (Italian / German / English) - and this is not a formality: the trilingual character is enforced both at the admission gate and inside the curriculum. The admission document states: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English.' The brochure 'At a Glance' box states: 'Courses will be taught in: Italian, German and English (trilingual)'. ACTUAL LANGUAGE SPLIT IN THE PUBLISHED 2026/27 COURSE OFFERING (each course on the unibz course-offering page carries an explicit EN / IT / DE tag; this is the hard evidence, not the marketing text): (a) FIRST YEAR, compulsory for ALL THREE study tracks - Economics for Accounting and Finance 12 CP EN (M-1 Macroeconomics EN, M-2 Industrial Economics EN); Applied Statistics for Accounting and Finance 6 CP EN; Advanced Accounting and Advanced Financial Statement Analysis 12 CP EN (both modules EN); AI and Computational Methods for Accounting and Finance 6 CP EN (Financial Analytics with AI EN, Blockchain/AI and Textual Methods EN); Financial Mathematics 6 CP EN; Advanced Corporate Finance (FIN I) 6 CP EN; and - decisively - ADVANCED BUSINESS LAW 6 CP taught in ITALIAN (course 25404, SSD GIUR-02/A, Prof. Paolo Giudici). So 48 of the 54 taught credit points of year one are in English, but 6 CP are compulsorily in Italian for every single student regardless of track. (b) SECOND YEAR - the language load depends entirely on the track. Professional Accounting and Auditing is the most Italian-intensive: Advanced Auditing 6 CP IT (25403), Advanced Taxation Law 6 CP IT (25406), Corporate Bankruptcy and Reorganization 6 CP IT (25414), Lab in CPA exam 3 CP IT (25431) = 21 CP of compulsory Italian, plus Italian-taught complementary options (Banking and Financial Law IT, Advanced Italian Accounting Standards IT). Finance and Financial Markets has RISK MANAGEMENT AND DERIVATIVES 6 CP taught in GERMAN (25437, Prof. Peter Alfons Schmid) as a compulsory course, plus AI and Financial Decision Making IT among the options. Business Administration and Consulting has LAB IN BUSINESS CONSULTING 3 CP taught in GERMAN (25454, Prof. Michael Nippa) as a compulsory course. Academic Writing and Research Skills 6 CP is EN in all tracks (25449, ANGL-01/C, Prof. Paolo Perego). (c) Free-choice courses published for 2026/27 are all English: Sustainability Accounting and Integrated Reporting EN, Business Intelligence and Data Visualization EN, International and EU Tax Law EN, CFA Preparation EN. SUMMARY: English is the dominant language of instruction (roughly two thirds to three quarters of the taught credits depending on track), Italian is a genuine and unavoidable second language of instruction (minimum 6 CP, up to ~27 CP in the accounting track), and German is the thinnest of the three (only 2 courses in the whole 2026/27 offering: 6 CP in the Finance track and 3 CP in the Consulting track). LANGUAGE-EXAM CHOICE RULES from the brochure: 'Students who graduated in a Ladin school in South Tyrol have to sit the English language exams and can choose between German or Italian for the others.' and 'Students who graduated in a language different from the three unibz official teaching languages must choose the two languages in which they intend to sit the language exams. They have to communicate their option to the Faculty Secretariat.' That second sentence is the one that matters for an international applicant: you must nominate TWO of the three languages, and English can only ever be one of them.
campus: Bozen-Bolzano - the main city-centre campus, Universitaetsplatz 1 / piazza Universita 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano, Italy. Confirmed by the brochure 'At a Glance' box ('Campus: Bozen-Bolzano') and by the Faculty of Economics and Management secretariat address. This is NOT the NOI Techpark campus (which hosts the Master in Software Engineering and Master in Computing for Data Science), NOT Brixen-Bressanone (Faculty of Education), NOT Bruneck-Brunico (Tourism, Sport and Event Management), and there is no Trento or Innsbruck component of the kind used by Energy Engineering or EMMA. Single-campus programme with no compulsory mobility. Optional mobility exists in two forms: (1) exchange programmes with selected European and international universities, and (2) the Double Degree with Baruch College (CUNY) and NYU Stern in New York, both of which are selective and taken after the first year. On-site facilities and the 24/7 emergency line for the Bozen-Bolzano city-centre campus: +39 0471 011011.
degree_class: LM-77 - Scienze economico-aziendali (Economics and Business Administration), the standard Italian second-cycle class for accounting/finance/management masters. Stated in the brochure 'At a Glance' box: 'Degree class: LM-77'. Practical consequence of the class code: under the national rule on simultaneous enrolment reproduced in the admission document, you may enrol in at most 2 programmes at the same time and the two may not belong to the same class, so you could not combine this with another LM-77 programme; the admission document illustrates the rule with the example 'LM-18/LM-18'. Note that the SSD (scientific-disciplinary sector) codes used in the entry requirements were renumbered by the 2024 Italian reform and the unibz document helpfully gives both the new and the old code for every sector (ECON-06/A ex SECS-P/07, ECON-07/A ex SECS-P/08, ECON-09/A ex SECS-P/09, ECON-09/B ex SECS-P/11, IEGE-01/A ex ING-IND/35). AlmaLaurea CODICIONE for this degree course: 0210107307800002.
admission_type: RESTRICTED ACCESS (numero programmato / numero chiuso) with a merit-based ranking list produced by documentary evaluation of the applicant's study career. There is NO entrance examination of any kind: no unibz written test, no TOLC, no TOLC-E, no CENT-S, no SAT, no aptitude test, no portfolio, no motivation letter, no project proposal, no video and no interview. Selection is a points-based dossier assessment out of a nominal 100 points built from four criteria (grade average, optional GMAT/GRE, above-minimum language proficiency, and prior attendance of courses that appear in this master's own curriculum), with a hard qualifying floor of 55 points. The language requirement operates as a separate ELIMINATORY gate before scoring: failing it excludes you from the procedure entirely and you appear in a bare exclusion table with no score at all. The curricular gate (degree class L-18/L-33 or 15 CP in the listed SSDs) works the same way. TWO SEPARATE RANKING LISTS are drawn up and published in the same signed decree: one for 'CITTADINI E CITTADINE UE ED EQUIPARATI/EQUIPARATE' (EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment) and one for 'CITTADINI E CITTADINE NON-UE RESIDENTI ALL'ESTERO' (non-EU citizens resident abroad). They do not compete with each other. The selection criteria were approved by the Faculty Council of the Faculty of Economics, resolution no. 142 of 15.09.2025 ('delibera del Consiglio di Facolta della Facolta di Economia n. 142 dd. 15.09.2025'), and the tie-break procedure is governed by art. 26, paragraph 2, letter b) of the university admission regulations in force. The admission committee for 2026/27 was chaired by Prof. Paolo Perego with Prof. Nicola Dalla Via and Prof. Massimiliano Bonacchi as members; the decrees are digitally signed and appealable to the Administrative Court of Bolzano within 60 days of notification or publication.
academic_requirements: You must hold ONE of two alternative qualifications. ROUTE 1 - a bachelor degree in one of the listed Italian degree classes, or an equivalent qualification gained abroad: under D.M. 270/04, L-18 Economics and Business Administration or L-33 Economics; under the older D.M. 509/99, class 17 Economics and Business Administration or class 28 Economic Sciences; or a 'Final degree or university certificate from a School of Economics, according to the regulation in force before M.D. 509/99'. Footnote in the admission document: 'Italian citizen who have obtained their degree abroad must also have a secondary school leaving qualification.' ROUTE 2 - a bachelor degree in ANY other class (or an equivalent foreign qualification) PROVIDED you have acquired at least 15 credit points in one or more of these scientific-disciplinary sectors, quoted with both the new post-2024-reform codes and their old equivalents: ECON-06/A (ex SECS-P/07) Accounting; ECON-07/A (ex SECS-P/08) Business Administration; ECON-09/A (ex SECS-P/09) Managerial Finance; ECON-09/B (ex SECS-P/11) Economics and Management of Financial Intermediary; IEGE-01/A (ex ING-IND/35) Industrial Engineering. Note that IEGE-01/A opens the door to engineering-management graduates, which is unusual for an LM-77. TWO ANTI-GAMING RULES attached to the 15 CP: 'Courses provided by the curriculum of the Master in Accounting and Finance are not taken into account for the achievement of the 15 credits required for admission to the Master programme', and 'Courses which are recognised for the achievement of the above-mentioned 15 CP cannot be used for a possible shortening of the study career.' So you cannot use this master's own courses to qualify for it, and credits spent on qualifying cannot later be recycled into credit recognition. FOR FOREIGN DEGREES the diploma supplement must demonstrate at least 180 ECTS AND that the qualification gives access to a master programme. Documentation must be in Italian, German or English and must state: final grade, exams passed with grade and date of passing, credit points, and (for foreign titles) the grading scale of the awarding university with the minimum pass grade and the maximum achievable grade. Scientific field codes are required only for Italian titles. 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary.' NOT-YET-GRADUATED APPLICANTS need at least 140 ECTS (see conditional_admission - note that 140 is higher than the 120 that most unibz masters require). COMPLETENESS IS ELIMINATORY: 'Only complete sets of documents will be evaluated. The absence of one or more documents required for the calculation of the grade average will result in exclusion from the ranking list.' 2026/27 EVIDENCE THAT THIS GATE BITES: the Early Bird decree contains a dedicated exclusion table for applicants who 'non sono in possesso e non stanno frequentando un corso di laurea nelle classi di laurea L-18 o L-33 e non raggiungono i 15 CFU negli ambiti disciplinari richiesti' - two applicants (IDs 144039 and 143880) were excluded on exactly this ground. LANGUAGE is a separate and equally eliminatory academic prerequisite - see language_requirements.
language_requirements: THE DECISIVE FIELD FOR THIS PROGRAMME. Verbatim from the admission document: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) 1st language: C1; 2nd language: B2; 3rd language: no level required. A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language. Exit level (to graduate) 1st language: C1; 2nd language: C1; 3rd language: B1.' THE POSITIONAL LOGIC: 'Your first language is the language in which you have the highest level of proficiency (C1). Your third language is instead the language in which you are weaker (or in which you are an absolute beginner).' The slots are assigned by your own strength, not by which language unibz prefers - but they must be filled from the set {German, Italian, English}, so English can occupy only one of the two certified slots. CERTIFICATION OBLIGATION: 'The certification is mandatory for the first and second language, for the third language it is recommended (from B1 onwards).' Certificates awarded by an Italian public institution are declared by self-declaration; those from a foreign public institution require an uploaded scanned copy of the original. Proof is submitted in the application portal under 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams', after creating an application under 'create/manage applications'. ELIMINATORY IN PRACTICE, not merely on paper - the 2026/27 decrees carry a dedicated exclusion table 'Le seguenti persone non soddisfano i requisiti linguistici richiesti per l'accesso e vengono pertanto escluse dal procedimento di ammissione': 7 EU/parity applicants excluded in the Early Bird session, 6 in the Late session, and BOTH non-EU applicants in the Early Bird session (the entire non-EU field). EU applicants excluded on language may re-apply in the second session and this genuinely works: applicant ID 155424 was excluded on language in the Early Bird session and then topped the Late Application ranking with 80.50 points. Non-EU applicants living abroad get no second chance because there is only one application window for them. DURING THE PROGRAMME: the third language must reach B1, otherwise you cannot register for the exams of courses taught in it - which is not hypothetical here, because Advanced Business Law (Italian) is compulsory for everyone and each track carries at least one further Italian- or German-taught compulsory course. Free Language Centre courses are provided: intensive A1 courses only in the September pre-semester window (01-18/09/2026, Monday to Friday, 6 hours a day), extensive courses of 4 hours a week during semesters, intensive courses of 8 hours a week between semesters, with the stated aim of reaching B1 in the third language after the first study year. TO GRADUATE: C1 in the first language, C1 in the second (up from B2 at entry) and B1 in the third. The second-language upgrade from B2 to C1 is a real workload item that applicants routinely overlook.
application_deadline_eu: THREE SESSIONS EXIST AT UNIBZ, BUT ONLY TWO ARE OPEN FOR THIS PROGRAMME. unibz publishes dates as DD/MM/YYYY; ISO equivalents given below. All cut-offs are 'by noon local time', i.e. 12:00 CET/CEST, not end of day. EARLY BIRD APPLICATION: 02/03 - 28/04/2026 = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28 (by noon). Language exams online 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026). Ranking lists by 27/05/2026. First instalment by 05/06/2026 noon. Enrolment 10/07 - 13/10/2026 noon. LATE APPLICATION (EU citizens only): 28/05 - 08/07/2026 = 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08 (by noon). Language exams online 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). Ranking lists by 30/07/2026. First instalment by 06/08/2026 noon. Enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 13/10/2026 noon. ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (EU citizens only), 18/08 - 04/09/2026 = 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04: NOT OFFERED FOR THIS PROGRAMME. The unibz Additional Application Session page lists 'Master in Accounting and Finance (Application NOT offered)' - one of only two programmes in the Faculty of Economics and Management shut out of that session, because the EU quota was filled. The admission-information PDF still carries the generic sentence 'The Faculty can open additional application sessions for single study programmes in August and in September if there are available places', but for 2026/27 the faculty did not open one here. MULTIPLE APPLICATIONS AND SECOND CHANCES: 'You might apply for more than one study programme. If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one.' This is real: applicant ID 155424 was excluded on language grounds in the Early Bird session and then finished FIRST in the Late Application ranking with 80.50 points. Conversely, three applicants (IDs 153444, 154698, 151823) were excluded on language in both sessions. There is no application fee for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE WINDOW ONLY, and it is the Early Bird: application 02/03 - 28/04/2026 = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, by noon local time. The admission document is categorical: 'Non-EU-Citizens (living outside of Italy). Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' There is no Late Application for non-EU citizens resident abroad (the Late session is labelled 'only for EU citizens'), and no Additional Application Session either generally for non-EU applicants or specifically for this programme. Missing 28 April 2026 means waiting a full year. APPLICATION FEE: 50 euro, non-refundable, described as an administration fee. Payable only by non-EU citizens living abroad. DOWNSTREAM DATES FOR THIS COHORT: ranking list by 27/05/2026; first instalment of 600 euro by 05/06/2026 noon to secure the place; then the compulsory Universitaly pre-enrolment and visa application; enrolment 10/07 - 13/10/2026 noon. THE SOBERING 2026/27 REALITY FOR THIS PROGRAMME: only 5 non-EU places existed, and none were filled. The non-EU section of the signed Early Bird decree contains no admissions table at all - only an exclusion table naming two applicant IDs (153960, 149873), both eliminated for failing the language requirement. A prospective non-EU applicant should read that as the programme being, in practice, unavailable from abroad without a certified Italian or German B2. Refund rule specific to this group: paying the first instalment is otherwise non-refundable, except 'for non-EU applicants living abroad who do not obtain the necessary documents for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country'.
required_documents: AT APPLICATION, uploaded in the online application portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup). (0) ACCOUNT AND IDENTITY: create an account and upload a valid ID card or passport, front and back. 'Please note: if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure.' (a) QUALIFICATION - if graduated in Italy: diploma supplement, or a self-declaration under Italian D.P.R. no. 445/2000 of the degree awarded with the exams passed (if graduated) or of the exams passed (if not yet graduated). If graduated abroad: diploma supplement or final degree certificate with exams passed (if graduated), or a transcript of records (if not yet graduated), in Italian, German or English. The document must contain: final grade; exams passed with grade and date of passing; credit points; scientific fields (for Italian titles only). For foreign qualifications additionally: 'scale of grades awarded by the university of provenance (with a minimum final grade to obtain the qualification and a maximum final grade achievable)' - omit this and the grade average cannot be computed, which means exclusion. The Faculty may also request course content descriptions and/or teaching hours. (b) EXCEL FILE - compulsory for non-graduates: 'If you have not graduated yet, you must confirm that you have acquired at least 140 credit points (ECTS) in your course of origin. Please use the excel file available in the application portal.' This is the structured upload; the template exists only inside the portal. (c) LANGUAGE CERTIFICATES - mandatory for the first and second language, recommended (from B1) for the third; additional certificates are also the vehicle for claiming the up-to-5 language points. Italian public-institution certificates go in as a self-declaration; foreign public-institution certificates as a scan of the original. Certificates that cannot be uploaded may be e-mailed as PDFs or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline. (d) GMAT and/or GRE CERTIFICATES - optional; unofficial GMAT score reports are accepted provisionally with the official report due by the first-instalment deadline. (e) SELF-DECLARATION of passed exams included in this master's curriculum - optional, used to claim the up-to-5 coursework points. (f) NON-EU CITIZENS RESIDENT IN ITALY claiming parity of treatment: a copy of the valid permit to stay (work, family, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons), plus the renewal request if it has expired. ELIMINATORY COMPLETENESS RULE: 'Only complete sets of documents will be evaluated. The absence of one or more documents required for the calculation of the grade average will result in exclusion from the ranking list.' And twice over: 'mendacious declarations will be sanctioned by criminal law and will result in your automatic exclusion'. Applications cannot be edited after submission. AT ENROLMENT, for holders of a foreign university degree: the bachelor degree diploma; an official translation into Italian (not required if issued in German or English); the diploma supplement showing at least 180 ECTS and that the qualification gives access to a master programme; plus the ARDI and/or CIMEA statements set out in credential_recognition. Until these are uploaded you remain admitted only with reservation.
entry_exam_or_test: NO ENTRANCE EXAM. There is no unibz admission test, no TOLC or TOLC-E, no CENT-S, no SAT and no subject test for this programme; admission is purely by dossier evaluation. Only two kinds of test appear anywhere in the procedure, and only one of them is compulsory. (1) OPTIONAL - GMAT or GRE. Explicitly not required: 'GMAT or GRE test: maximum 20 points. It contributes to the calculation of the overall score, but is not a compulsory requirement for the admission.' Scoring: GMAT 0-490 = 0 points, 491-650 = 8 points, above 650 = 20 points; GRE 0-300 = 0 points, 301-327 = 8 points, above 327 = 20 points. Validity: 'The GMAT test will only be scored if it has been passed with a score above 490 in the 5 years preceding the selection process.' 'The GRE test will only be considered as an alternative to the GMAT test if it has been taken with a score above 300 in the 5 years preceding the selection process.' Unofficial score reports are accepted at application: 'The committee will also consider any unofficial GMAT score reports, and applicants agree to submit the official report no later than the deadline for payment of the first instalment' (i.e. 05/06/2026 for Early Bird, 06/08/2026 for Late). GMAT is booked at www.mba.com and GRE at www.ets.org/gre/. (2) COMPULSORY IN EFFECT - LANGUAGE PROFICIENCY. You must prove C1 in a first and B2 in a second official teaching language. If you do not already hold a recognised certificate or a qualifying school/university medium of instruction, the only remaining route is the unibz Language Centre proficiency exam, which is held online on fixed dates: for the Early Bird session, 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); for the Late Application session, 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). Two restrictions catch people out: 'you can only register for C1 and B2 level exams' and 'only for one level per language (e.g. in the same exam session you can register for a C1 German and a B2 Italian exam, but not for a C1 and a B2 German exam)'. Registration opens only inside the windows above and only after you have created an application in the portal. There are NO Language Centre exams for the Additional Application Session - which is moot for this programme, since it is not open in that session. (3) A third test exists but only AFTER admission and it does not affect selection: a placement test in the third language for admitted students who cannot certify it, used to assign them to a learning path towards B1.
tuition_or_fees_link: Faculty of Economics and Management fees page: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/economics-management/fees (Italian/German-only 'Tuition Fees Regulation' linked from it). AMOUNT: approximately 1,200 euro per year, in two instalments. 'Fees amount to 1200 euro. 1st instalment (600 euro): includes the revenue stamp of 16 euro. 2nd instalment (600 euro): must be paid by March of the following year.' The faculty fees page dates the second instalment precisely at 31 March 2027 for the 2026/27 year. TIMING NUANCE THAT CONFUSES NEW STUDENTS: the faculty page states the first instalment is due 'by 13 October 2026', but a NEWLY ADMITTED applicant must pay it much earlier - by 05/06/2026 noon (Early Bird) or 06/08/2026 noon (Late) - because that payment is what secures the place in the ranking list. The October date applies to continuing students. PENALTIES: delayed payment triggers a 30-euro fine and an automatic block on your online account, which means no access to mySNS, no exam registration and no transfer to another university or programme until it is cleared. FUORI CORSO SURCHARGE: students who exceed the normal length of the programme pay 900 euro for the first instalment (a 300-euro surcharge) from the second year beyond normal length; repeated years count towards the calculation, interruption years do not. GRADUATION-TIMING RELIEF: if you sit the final exam by 31 October you do not pay for the new academic year; if you graduate after October but by 31 March you select 'I will graduate by 31 March' on the payment page and pay only a virtual 16-euro duty stamp (with the full year's fees plus late fine becoming due if you then fail or postpone). EXEMPTIONS: total exemption (16-euro stamp only) for students with a disability recognised under article 3 paragraph 1 of Law 104/1992 or an invalidity of 66% or more, on submission of the health-authority certificate; and, on request, for foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship. Holders of a South Tyrol provincial grant are reimbursed the fees paid for the year (late-payment fines are not reimbursed), typically with the first instalment refunded between March and April. NO REFUNDS on dropping out, interrupting studies or being excluded. Payment is made via pagoPA payment slip after an e-mail invitation from the Student Office; receipts are downloadable as PDFs.

official_call_url: [uncertain] No separate 'call for applications', bando or manifesto degli studi is published in English for this programme. The role of an official call is performed jointly by three documents. (1) The admission-information PDF, https://www.unibz.it/assets/CoursesPDF/master-in-accounting-and-finance_admission-information_en_GB.pdf - the operative document carrying deadlines, quotas, entry requirements, the scoring rubric and the enrolment rules. (2) The two signed ranking-list decrees, which restate the full selection criteria, the tie-break rules, the enrolment obligations and the appeal route, and are the only legally signed instruments in the process: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Ranking-Lists/2026-Early-Bird/Ranking-List-Master-in-Accounting-and-Finance-Early-Bird-Session.pdf and https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Ranking-Lists/2026-Late-application/Ranking-List-Master-in-Accounting-and-Finance-Late-Session.pdf . Both are bilingual Italian/German only - no English version exists. (3) The underlying governance acts, which are cited but not published as standalone downloadable files: the resolution of the Faculty Council of the Faculty of Economics no. 142 of 15.09.2025 approving the selection criteria, and the university admission regulations in force (art. 26 paragraph 2 letter b) governing tie-breaks). Faculty regulations are browsable, in German and Italian only, through the unibz records portal at https://records-unibz.siavcloud.com/regolamenti_en?area=FACULTY%20OF%20ECONOMICS%20AND%20MANAGEMENT&priority=02&orderasc=sub_area , and signed administrative acts are published on the online notice board https://records-unibz.siavcloud.com/albo_online_en . uncertainty_notes: DATA VINTAGE. Everything here is the 2026/27 admission cycle, captured on 2026-08-29 from documents whose own footer reads 'Subject to change. Latest update: 24.08.2026'. Both 2026/27 ranking lists are final and signed, so the cycle is effectively closed: the Early Bird and Late deadlines have passed and this programme is NOT open in the Additional Application Session. A candidate reading this now is planning for 2027/28, and quotas, deadlines, the language-exam calendar, the GMAT/GRE bands and the provincial grant amounts are all re-set annually. Re-verify against the 2027/28 admission-information PDF when it appears (typically from late 2026 / early 2027). WHAT IS SOLID: teaching languages, entry and exit language levels, entry requirements including the 15 CP SSD list, the 140 ECTS conditional threshold, the full scoring rubric and 55-point threshold, all quotas and deadlines, the fee structure, and every 2026/27 outcome statistic - all taken directly from the admission-information PDF, the brochure and the two signed ranking-list decrees, which for once do not contradict each other (the brochure simply reprints the admission text as pages 10-20). WHAT IS INFERRED, NOT QUOTED: (1) the expansion of the internal curriculum codes 'curr. LP', 'curr. FIN' and 'curr. DCA' to the three named study tracks - the mapping follows from which courses carry which tag, but unibz publishes no glossary; (2) the credit-weighted English/Italian/German proportions, which I computed from the per-course EN/IT/DE tags on the 2026/27 course-offering page rather than from any official statement of the language split; (3) the reading that the Late session admitting 20 against a 10-place quota reflects the published carry-over rule, which is the only mechanism that explains the number but is not stated in the decree. KNOWN GAPS. The exact year the programme was first activated is not published in English. The Faculty Council resolution 142 of 15.09.2025 and the university admission regulations (art. 26(2)(b)) are cited in the decrees but have no resolvable public URL; faculty regulations are browsable only in German and Italian through the records portal. Double Degree scholarship amounts, the number of awards and the internal selection format for Baruch/NYU Stern are not published. Provincial merit-scholarship thresholds and amounts are not on the unibz pages. Three former study-plan URLs indexed by search engines (study-plan-professional-accounting-and-auditing and its two siblings) now return 404; the live study plan is rendered dynamically inside the programme page, so the brochure is the reliable source for track structure. MINOR INTERNAL INCONSISTENCIES IN THE SOURCES: the brochure prints Internship as 5 CP in the Business Administration and Consulting track but 6 CP in the other two - almost certainly a typo, since all three tracks must total 120 ECTS. Four courses in the 2026/27 offering carry no language tag at all (Financial Engineering and Quantitative Investment Strategies, Issues in CPA profession, Lab in Financial Trading, both Modeling Financial Statement variants, Internship), so their language is unknown and my credit-weighted split treats them as unassigned. The faculty fees page dates the first instalment 13 October 2026 while newly admitted students must pay by 5 June or 6 August - both are correct but for different populations. The programme page contains the typo 'definetely'. LANGUAGE OF THE BINDING DOCUMENTS: the ranking-list decrees - the only signed legal acts in the procedure, and the only place the actual scores, cut-offs and exclusion grounds appear - exist solely in Italian and German. An English-only applicant cannot read the very documents that decide their case, which is itself a fair summary of this programme's accessibility problem. NOT VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: the AlmaLaurea 93% employment figure and the Times Higher Education 2025 subject-ranking placements are unibz marketing claims reproduced from the brochure; I did not check them against AlmaLaurea or THE directly.
